title: Turn a Codex exploration into a published Deepnote app
summary: See the latest product updates and improvements to Deepnote.
body_markdown:
## [June 4, 2026](https://deepnote.com/changelog/2026-06-04)


#


[Deepnote is now in OpenAI Codex](https://deepnote.com/changelog/2026-06-04#deepnote-is-now-in-openai-codex)


Codex now connects natively to your Deepnote workspace. The context your team has already built — notebooks, scheduled analyses, data apps, and integrations — is available to Codex directly, so any exploration starts from your real work.


Watch this demo, where we connect Codex to a live workspace and run a fraud detection project end to end — summarizing projects, serving a model, auto-running the card-cancellation workflow, and writing a new analysis back into Deepnote.


Codex connects via the[Deepnote MCP](https://deepnote.com/docs/deepnote-mcp) and operates within your existing permissions: it can search for projects, read and run notebooks, write new ones, and inspect integrations.


Here's what that unlocks:


###


[Your workspace as the context for every exploration](https://deepnote.com/changelog/2026-06-04#your-workspace-as-the-context-for-every-exploration)


Most real questions cross team boundaries. Codex can now search and read across every project in your workspace, pulling from the marketing, sales, and product notebooks to compose a single answer across all three — built on how your team already defines and measures things.


###


[Turn a Codex exploration into a published Deepnote app](https://deepnote.com/changelog/2026-06-04#turn-a-codex-exploration-into-a-published-deepnote-app)


An exploration doesn't have to end as a chat thread. Because Codex can write back to Deepnote, you can share its work as a notebook or a published app your team can open, rerun, and extend.


###


[Build and refine real workflows](https://deepnote.com/changelog/2026-06-04#build-and-refine-real-workflows)


Codex can interact with individual blocks in your notebooks, so you build persistent, production-ready workflows instead of one-off queries — adding features to a model, tuning thresholds, or dropping in monitoring over a few targeted prompts.


##


[Connect Deepnote to Codex](https://deepnote.com/changelog/2026-06-04#connect-deepnote-to-codex)


1. Open Codex
2. Select Plugins and find[Deepnote](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/share/449d4e5659914849bfdf87e5c6d51960)
3. Click Enabled in Codex, then Connect
4. Follow the OAuth flow and select a workspace


Deepnote is live in the[Codex data analytics plugin today](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/share/449d4e5659914849bfdf87e5c6d51960) . The Deepnote MCP and[public API](https://deepnote.com/docs/deepnote-api) behind this connection open up a lot more opportunities — more on that soon!
